findings.reason: The protected implementation is the optimal runtime solution for the deliberately finite source domain. Its named eight-value residues tuple exhausts every legal n from 1 through 8 and the n - 1 lookup is direct, conventional, constant-time, and free of unnecessary control flow or naming defects, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 479, its Python integer method, and its runnable solve(n) adapter. The lookup accepts exactly the source's eight digit counts and returns the residue of the largest palindromic product of two n-digit integers, with maximization conceptually preceding reduction modulo 1337.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2064993265 are algorithmically identical: both define the same ordered residue tuple and return residues[n - 1]. Their only structural difference is the native Solution.largestPalindrome wrapper.

The mandated original-blocker playbook classifies frontend ID 479 as bounded_domain because legal n has only eight values. The verified certificate records workload maximum 8, a bounded-work proof for one table access, and exhaustive-domain replacement evidence; no completed benchmark coexists with it. The exact current source passed all 8 opaque legal-input executions with runtime_check false, complexity_check true, method bounded_domain, and complexity_passed true.

Runtime performs one subtraction and one access into a fixed eight-entry tuple, so both time and storage are O(1). Any mirrored-palindrome or factor enumeration belongs only to offline derivation of the immutable finite table and is not executed by the submitted algorithm. The strict certificate validator and its all-non-scaling-certificate regression pass.

The current-targeted Approach exactly explains the finite-domain lookup, why the eight entries preserve the mathematical maximum, how they may be independently derived by descending mirrored-palindrome factor search, and why that derivation is excluded from runtime complexity. Its modulo-order and domain-bound edge cases match the protected source.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the two n-digit-factor requirement, largest-palindrome objective, final modulo 1337 operation, both examples in source order, the complete 99 * 91 = 9009 and modulo explanation for Example 1, the absence of an Example 2 explanation, the sole 1 <= n <= 8 constraint, and the absence of visuals, tables, or later sections.
